body.text: In short:
An 11-year-old boy remains in a critical condition after being shot in the face at a Norwest home in Sydney's north-west.
Police are investigating if men present at the time of the incident have links to organised crime.
An 18-year-old man has been charged with concealing a serious indictable offence.
Link copied Share Share article Police are investigating whether men present at the time an 11-year-old boy was shot in the head at a north-west Sydney home had links to organised crime.
The child was treated for wounds to the face and neck and remains in a critical condition in hospital, following the incident at a Norwest home about 5pm on Monday.
Isaac Bechara, 18, has been charged with concealing a serious indictable offence, with two other men, both aged 18, released from custody after being questioned by police.
Police are investigating possible organised crime links. ( ABC News )
A 43-year-old woman was also present at the time of the shooting, with another person not yet located.
Mr Bechara did not apply for bail but it was formally refused at a hearing in Blacktown Local Court on Tuesday morning.
The matter has been adjourned until next month.
Some witnesses 'not co-operating'
Investigators are looking into whether the men inside the unit have links to organised crime.
Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Superintendent Naomi Moore said police had "engaged" with the young boy's family before when asked about their underworld links.
"Police have engaged with the occupants previously and again that's all I want to say about that at the moment," she said.
" However, a number of individuals that were inside the unit at the time are well known to NSW Police and their association with organised crime is being considered by investigators. "
Superintendent Moore provided an update on Tuesday. ( ABC News )

Some of those present at the home last night "are not co-operating with investigators", Superintendent Moore added and that others were being sought by detectives after they fled before police arrived.
"A number of people did leave before the police arrived, and we are hoping to speak to them shortly," she said.
Police on Monday night had said there was no evidence to suggest the incident was related to underworld tensions.
"We have nothing to suggest that it is organised crime-related, but we will conduct a very thorough investigation into this," Superintendent Moore said.
"For those that are obviously fearful on the streets out here at the moment, we are content that we are doing a very thorough investigation here."
She said the boy's mother was with him in hospital and was "distressed, as any parent would be".
Superintendent Moore also said police had not yet recovered the firearm.
'Horrible event'
Emergency vehicles were at the scene on Monday afternoon. ( ABC News )
A resident at the unit block said police could be seen searching a nearby park and creek after the shooting.
"They had cordoned off the whole park at that time, and they were searching … until late in the night, I believe," he said.
Premier Chris Minns on Tuesday described the incident as an "incredibly distressing situation".
"It's also a very a tragic reminder of how dangerous guns are, often the people who are the victims of guns are innocent people," he said.
